taskDescription: Arrange the steps of bilirubin metabolism in the correct order, from haem degradation to faecal pigment.
paragraphs: Macrophages in the spleen break down old red cells, and haem oxygenase converts haem to biliverdin.
Biliverdin reductase reduces biliverdin to unconjugated bilirubin, which is water-insoluble.
Unconjugated bilirubin travels in plasma bound to albumin and cannot pass into urine.
The hepatocyte takes up bilirubin and conjugates it with glucuronic acid using UGT1A1.
Water-soluble conjugated bilirubin is pumped into the bile canaliculus and reaches the gut.
Gut bacteria convert conjugated bilirubin to urobilinogen; the remainder colours the stool as stercobilin.

overallFeedback.feedback: Bilirubin moves from macrophage (unconjugated, albumin-bound, cannot enter urine) to hepatocyte (conjugated, water-soluble, enters bile) to gut (urobilinogen and stercobilin). This sequence explains why haemolysis raises unconjugated bilirubin without bilirubinuria, while biliary obstruction raises conjugated bilirubin with dark urine and pale stools.
